about: Physics blocks whose maths is a formula (ND3b): each keeps its id, ports and results, and its maths is the Equation below, with a name that says what happens.

params.description: Koch and Motz's constant, per MeV

references: Koch, H. W. and Motz, J. W. 1959, Bremsstrahlung cross-section formulas and related data, Rev. Mod. Phys. 31, 920: the share of an electron's energy radiated as it stops in a material of atomic number Z, Y = k Z T / (1 + k Z T) with k about 6e-4 per MeV. doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.31.920

Hubbell, J. H. and Seltzer, S. M. 2004, Tables of X-ray mass attenuation coefficients and mass energy-absorption coefficients (NIST Standard Reference Database 126): aluminium and liquid water. https://physics.nist.gov/PhysRefData/XrayMassCoef/
atoms.shown: Y = k Z T / (1 + k Z T)

equation.name: Share of a stopped electron's energy given off as X-rays
equation.formula:
x = k * Z * max(E, 0)
Y = x / (1 + x)

k.name: Koch and Motz's constant, per MeV

Y.name: share of its energy given off as X-rays

source.text: Koch, H. W. and Motz, J. W. 1959, Rev. Mod. Phys. 31, 920

explain.curious: An electron stopped in metal shakes out X-rays as it slows. Behind a thick wall those X-rays, not the electrons, give most of the dose, so a heavier wall helps less than you would hope.
explain.science: The radiation yield of a stopping electron, used with Kramers' flat thick-target spectrum and the NIST photon coefficients for the shield and tissue to give the bremsstrahlung dose behind a shield.

params.description: the belt's pitch-angle anisotropy, the same figure the belt model grows its waves with (A in sin^(2A) of the pitch angle); 0 is the same in every direction

references: Roederer, J. G. 1970, Dynamics of Geomagnetically Trapped Radiation, Springer (Physics and Chemistry in Space 2): Liouville's theorem along a field line, so a pitch-angle spread sin^n of the equatorial angle keeps its shape and scales as (B_eq / B)^(n/2). doi:10.1007/978-3-642-49300-3

Walt, M. 1994, Introduction to Geomagnetically Trapped Radiation, Cambridge University Press, chapter 3: the dipole field along a line, B / B_eq = sqrt(1 + 3 sin^2 lat) / cos^6 lat. doi:10.1017/CBO9780511524981

equation.name: How a belt thins away from the magnetic equator along its field line
equation.formula:
c = abs(cos(lat))
S = if c <= 0 then 0 else (c^6 / sqrt(1 + 3 * sin(lat)^2))^A

lat.name: magnetic latitude on the field line, radians

S.name: share of the equator's dose left at this latitude

source.where: Liouville mapping on a dipole line

explain.curious: Trapped particles bounce up and down their field line, but most turn back before they get far from the equator. So the belt is thickest at the equator and thins towards the poles, which is why probes come in over the poles.
explain.science: For a directional flux sin^(2A) of the equatorial pitch angle, Liouville's theorem gives the omnidirectional flux at latitude λ on a dipole line as (B_eq/B)^A of its equatorial value, B/B_eq = √(1+3 sin²λ)/cos⁶λ. A stand-in for a real pitch-angle model; the loss cone is not cut.
